key_insight: Global optimal control can strongly suppress decoherence in globally driven superconducting quantum processors by reshaping the drive, rather than isolating a protected subsystem.
engineering_relevance: For ladder-style superconducting architectures, temporally optimized global pulses can shorten gate sequences by about an order of magnitude while preserving high-fidelity one- and two-qubit operations.
method: Model a quasi-two-dimensional ladder geometry as a prototype globally driven superconducting architecture.
Use tensor-network simulations to track how amplitude damping and dephasing affect information flow and gate fidelity.
Optimize the global control waveform to compress gate timing and mitigate decoherence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tensor-network-based evaluation of information transport and gate fidelities under amplitude-damping and dephasing, showing that optimized drive shaping restores high fidelities and reduces gate times by roughly 10x.
watch_item: Because dissipation acts on all physical qubits in the globally driven device, the approach depends on precise control waveform design and may be sensitive to hardware imperfections.
paper_title: Mitigating quantum decoherence via global optimal control
